column2: Thus, in order, one should purify the body by drying and the like; one should meditate on the dried body from the feet to the end of the crest.
With the seed Yam and the seed Vam, the body joined with a garland of flames; with the syllable Ram it goes out through the Brahma-aperture.
Having meditated on a drop of nectar, with that one should flood the ash-body; from the syllable Lam, preparing a divine body,
having done placement on hand and body, one should perform the mental worship: Vishnu with limbs in the lotus of the heart, with mental flowers and the rest.
With the root-mantra one should worship the lord of gods, giver of enjoyment and liberation: "Welcome, lord of the gods of gods; be present, Keshava.
Accept the mental worship as truly contemplated." Then the support-power, the tortoise, Ananta is to be worshipped, then the earth.

In the middle and in the fire direction and others, dharma and the rest, adharma and the rest led by Indra; sattva and the rest, the lotus in the middle, in the principle called illusion and ignorance,
the principle of time, the orb of the sun and others, the king of birds; in the middle then, from Vayavya to Ishana, the line of teachers.
The Gana, Sarasvati are to be worshipped, Narada, Nalakubara; the teacher, the teacher's sandals, the supreme teacher and sandals,
the earlier perfected ones and later perfected ones, and in the filaments the powers: Lakshmi, Sarasvati, Priti, Kirti, Shanti and Kantika,
Pushti, Tushti, Mahendra and the others; in the middle Hari, invoked by speech; Dhriti, Shri, Rati, Kanti and others; Achyuta established by the root-mantra.
Om, face me, praying thus "Be present"; having placed and given arghya and the rest, one should worship with scent and the rest by the root-mantra.
Om, frighten, frighten — heart; "terrify again" — head; "crush, crush" — crest, in the fire direction and the rest, the missile from the weapon.
Protect, protect, destroy, destroy — armor, then homage; "Om Hrum phat" — homage to the missile; with the root seed also the limb.
In the east, south, west and north one should worship the enclosure of forms: Vasudeva, Sankarshana, Pradyumna and Aniruddha.
In the fire direction and others, the forms of Hari: Shri, Dhriti, Rati and Kanti; the conch, discus, mace and lotus in the fire direction and the others, beginning in the east.
The Sharnga bow, pestle, sword and forest-garland outside it; Indra and the others, and Ananta in the southwest, then Varuna;
Brahma between Indra and Ishana; the enclosure of missiles outside; Airavata, then the goat, buffalo, monkey, fish,
deer, hare, bull, tortoise, swan — then outside; Prishnigarbha, Kumuda and others as door-guards, two and two;
from the east to the north door, having bowed to Hari, an offering outside; "Homage to Vishnu's attendants" — one should give the offering on the offering-seat.
One should worship Vishvaksena in Ishana for the universe; one should tie the protective thread on the god's right hand.
Teachers of the year, to the giver of the complete fruit; for the mounting of the sacred thread, hold this charm. Om, homage.
One should perform the vow of fasting and the rest in the presence of the god: "Restrained by fasting and the rest, I satisfy the god.
May desire, anger and the rest not stay with me at all, from today, lord of gods, until the special day."

If the sacrificer is weak, the vower may do a night-meal and the like. Having offered and dismissed after praising, the Shrikara daily worship: "Om Hrim Shrim, homage to Shridhara, enchanter of the three worlds."
That is the womb of all beings and of the group of knowledge-mantras; fire is the cause of liberation, the Supreme Self, giver of liberation.
In the east the head is declared; the arms are established in the corners; in the northeast and southeast corners the shanks; in the northwest and southwest too.
The belly is called the fire-pit; the yoni is laid down as the yoni; the three qualities are the girdles; having thus meditated, ten fuel sticks.
One should offer fifteen more with Om by the fist-mudra; again one should offer the two Aghara streams, ending with Vayu and Agni, then cook.
Ending with Ishana, with the root-mantra one should offer the two ghee portions; in the north with the twelve-ending, in the south with that, in the middle.
With the utterance, one should meditate on the fire purified, standing in the middle of the lotus: the Vaishnava, seven-tongued, shining like a crore of suns.
Moon-faced and sun-eyed, one should offer a hundred and eight; half that with the root, eight; and a tenth for the limbs.
Having worshipped with scent and the rest, with scent, flowers and rice and the rest, one should offer to Hari with the root-mantra beginning "Vishnu-tejas."
Having then given at the fire's place, one should pray to the god: "You whose body lies on the couch of the great serpent in the milk ocean,
in the morning I shall worship you; be present, Keshava." Then having given an offering to Indra and others and to Vishnu's attendants,
then in front of the god a pot with a pair of garments, with water mixed with rochana, camphor, saffron, scent and the like,
adorned with scent and flowers, one should worship with the root-mantra; coming outside the pavilion, in three anointed circles,
the five cow-products, the porridge and the tooth-stick are in order; reciting the Purana, praise and keeping vigil at night,
for servants of others, children, women and those who enjoy pleasures, one should do the immediate dwelling without scent and thread.
From the little finger and so on to the god, and the forest garland from the root; from the heart-mantra to Vishvaksena one should offer the sacred threads.
Having offered in the fire and to the fire-wick-bearers, to Vishnu and others, having worshipped the thread, one should give the full oblation for atonement from the root.
Or a hundred and eight, with the five Upanishads; with garlands of jewels and coral, with mandara flowers and the rest.

May this yearly worship be yours, O Garuda-bannered; as the forest-garland, god, and the Kaustubha are ever on your heart,
agnipuran:36:15	so bear the sacred threads and the worship on your heart. Whatever has been done in the vow-worship, willingly or unwillingly,
agnipuran:36:16	by rule, with obstacles removed, may that be complete for me. Having prayed, bowed and asked pardon, one should place the thread on the head.
Having given the offering, one should satisfy the Vaishnava teacher with fees; the Brahmins with food, clothes and the rest for a day or a fortnight.
At bathing time one should take down the thread and offer it. One should give food without hindrance and eat oneself.
On the day of dismissal, having worshipped, one should dismiss the threads: "Having duly completed this yearly worship of mine,
go now, sacred thread, dismissed, to Vishnu's world." Having worshipped in the middle of Soma and Isha, and Vishvaksena of that,
having worshipped the threads one should present them to a Brahmin. As many strands as are set in that thread,
so many thousands of ages he is honored in Vishnu's world. Having uplifted a hundred families, ten before and ten after, and established them in Vishnu's world, he himself attains liberation.
For purification, giving the fruit of a year's worship: "Homage to you, Shiva-deva; accept this sacred thread."
For purification, giving the fruit of a year's worship: "Homage to you, Baneshvara; accept this sacred thread."
For purification, giving the fruit of a year's worship: "Homage to you, Shakti-deva; accept this sacred thread."
For purification, giving the fruit of a year's worship: the thread made of Narayana, the excellent made of Aniruddha,
giving wealth, grain, life and health I give to you. The thread made of Kamadeva, the excellent made of Sankarshana,
giving knowledge, offspring and good fortune I give to you. The thread made of Vasudeva, giving dharma, desire, wealth and liberation,
I give to you, the cause of crossing the ocean of the world. The thread made of the universal form, giving all, destroying sin,
I give to you the uplift of families past and future. The four beginning with the little finger he gave in order with the mantras.
The builder of Vishnu's dwelling gets threefold the fruit as stated; with arrangements of bandhuka flowers, with nectar-like plaster, the Vaishnava temple,
those who plaster the house go to the city of the Lord. Fallen, falling or half-fallen — a man
who restores Hari's abode gains double the fruit. He who builds a fallen one and protects a fallen one
of Vishnu's dwelling here, the man shares Vishnu's world. As long as the mass of bricks stays in Hari's temple,
the builder with his family is honored in Vishnu's world. He alone is virtuous and to be honored here and hereafter.
He who has a banner made for Krishna Vasudeva — he alone is born righteous; his family is purified by that.
The builder of a house for Vishnu, Rudra, the Sun, the Goddess and others gains fame. What use to that fool is a heap of wealth guarded,
earned with pain, who does not have a house made for Krishna? Whose wealth is not enjoyable by the ancestors, Brahmins and gods,
not for the enjoyment of kin, his gaining of wealth is vain. As death is certain for men, so loss of wealth is certain.
The fool clings to it in this fleeting, hollow life. When wealth is not for giving or for the enjoyment of embodied beings,
nor for fame nor dharma, what virtue is there in owning it? Therefore, having gained wealth by fate or by effort,
one should rightly give to the best Brahmins and have monuments made; because it is better than gifts, better than monuments;
therefore the wise should have a temple of Vishnu and others built; having installed Hari's abode with devoted best of men,
the whole three worlds with the moving and unmoving are installed: past, future and present, gross, subtle and other,
from Brahma to a blade of grass, all is the arising of Vishnu. Having installed a dwelling for that god of gods, all-pervading, great-souled,
one is not born again on earth. As is the fruit in making Vishnu's abode, so for the gods.
